title: Second Opium War
key_facts: Renewed conflict involving Britain and France against Qing China
Sparked by the Arrow incident and disputes over treaty enforcement and diplomatic rights
Allied capture of Canton and Tianjin; Anglo-French march on Beijing
causes: Disputes over execution of the Treaty of Nanjing and access to the interior
Arrow incident (1856) used as a casus belli by the British
French involvement following the killing of a missionary and broader imperial aims
outcome: Treaties of Tianjin (1858) and Convention of Beijing (1860) expanding foreign privileges
Legalization of the opium trade and opening of additional treaty ports
Sacking of the Old Summer Palace (Yuanmingyuan) by Anglo-French forces
impacts: Further erosion of Qing sovereignty and deepening foreign influence
Greater missionary access and residence in Beijing
Integration of China into 19th-century global trade systems under unequal terms
